blocks.x: Underwriting copilot with cited evidence, medical-evidence reading time down 65% and risk density up 23% at flat mortality assumptions

A life insurer: Insurers feel process gaps in loss adjustment expense and customer churn, both of them slow, both of them measurable. The Achala program started with the claims journey —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
The baseline month measured the reading: 71% of case handling time was evidence extraction, and two underwriters given the same file produced different debits 19% of the time.
Evidence arrived unstructured and unlinked; the underwriting system recorded the decision but not the reading. Audit reviewed outcomes and hoped the reasoning was consistent.

We built the copilot on retrieval with evaluation gates: every document parsed into structured evidence with each finding cited to its page, debits proposed against the codified manual, and an evaluation harness scoring extraction quality against senior-underwriter reads before the copilot saw live cases. The underwriter decides with the citations attached; the file carries both.
